value.body: Two-year postgraduate diplomas after MBBS in a specialty such as anaesthesia (DA), obstetrics and gynaecology (DGO), paediatrics (DCH), ophthalmology (DO) or ENT (DLO). They give specialist training in less time than a three-year MD/MS, but with a narrower scope and fewer teaching-post options.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Versus 3 years for MD/MS or DNB

items.label: NMC phase-out
items.value: Medical-college PG diploma seats to convert to MD/MS seats from 2027-28

items.label: NBEMS post-MBBS diplomas
items.note: 8 broad specialties notified in 2020; NBEMS says the NMC notice does not apply to them

value.title: How you get in
value.body: MBBS with internship and registration, then NEET-PG. Medical-college diploma seats are allotted through MCC and state counselling; NBEMS diploma seats at accredited hospitals go through NBEMS / MCC counselling.

value.title: At a glance
items: With medical-college diplomas being converted to MD/MS, the diploma route is shrinking — check what is on offer in your counselling year.
Diploma holders can take a two-year post-diploma DNB (entry via DNB-PDCET, run by NBEMS) to reach degree level.
Diploma holders can practise as specialists, but faculty posts in medical colleges generally need an MD/MS/DNB.
